chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hudhayl ibn Hanan, brother of Ja'far ibn Hanan al-Sayrafī, said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I have entrusted to my brother Ja'far ibn Hanan some wealth that was mine, and he gives me what I spend, and I perform Hajj with it and give charity. I have asked those from our side, and they mentioned that this is invalid and not permissible. I wish to refer to your opinion in this matter, so what do you say?
He said: 'Did he give you (money) before you entrusted your wealth to him?' I said: 'Yes.'

He said: 'Take from him what he gives you, eat from it, drink from it, give charity from it, and perform Hajj with it. So when you arrive in Iraq, say: Indeed, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) gave me a fatwa regarding this.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on entrusting money to a family member for management and spending?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic distinction between a loan (qard) and a trust (amanah) in the context of familial financial management. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the arrangement by verifying that the brother was already providing for the narrator's expenses prior to the transfer, thereby treating the incoming funds as permissible sustenance rather than a debt to be repaid in kind. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding intra-family economic support, emphasizing the continuity of benefit over strict contractual formality.
